title: Comparison of various radiation-free methods for attenuation correction (AC) in pediatric examinations on the Biograph Vision Quadra (PET/CT)
summary:
For children and adolescents with cancer, it is important to choose a appropriate imaging modality for diagnosis. A careful risk assessment needs to be carried out, especially for children who often need to be examined regularly, for example to monitor treatment. The clinical question, the child's developmental stage, the required examination time and radiation dose, and the need for anaesthesia all play a role.
Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) is ideal for assessing local findings and metastases because of its high soft tissue contrast. It works without radiation. However, positron emission tomography (PET) has a higher specificity for tumour tissue. PET measures the three-dimensional distribution of a previously injected, low-level radioactive substance - called a "tracer" - in the body. The tracer is usually a radioactively labelled sugar variant that accumulates more in tumour cells than in healthy tissue. This type of imaging is associated with low radiation exposure. However, a PET scan must always be combined with a parallel second examination in order to calculate the PET image data (= attenuation correction). Attenuation correction is a prerequisite for a well-interpreted PET image, as otherwise the activity distribution of the tracer will show distorted image values due to the different tissue densities. There are several options for radiation-free attenuation correction, but these have not been studied in detail in children. The aim of the study is to test these alternative methods of calculating PET image data for children.

interventions.name: Children/adolescents in whom an additional dose-neutral attenuation correction (LSO-TX) is performed on clinically indicated PET/CT for CT-based attenuation correction.

Children/adolescents who have undergone PET/MR and who require CT. The attenuation map generated by the MR Dixon sequence on the MRI scanner is transferred to correct the emission data from the PET/CT scanner (MR-Reg).

Children/adolescents for whom a PET is indicated and is performed as part of a PET/CT or PET/MRI scan. In this case, the attenuation map is also generated using only on the PET emission data (Synthetic-AI CT).

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Children/adolescents <18 years of age who have undergone a whole-body MRI and are to undergo a PET scan with the Biograph Vision Quadra for clinical indications (usually staging and restaging, risk stratification for malignant tumours),
or
children/adolescents aged <18 years who are to undergo a clinically indicated PET/MRI and who also require a high-contrast, low-dose CT scan of the lungs and bones for clinical indications,
or
children/adolescents aged <18 years who are to undergo a clinically indicated PET scan, but who also require a low-dose CT scan for morphological classification of the expected findings.
In addition, written consent should always be obtained from the legal guardian and, if appropriate, the child.
Exclusion criteria:
pregnancy
